headline: Payrolls beat by 100,000 and revive Fed hike bets: dollar posts its best day since June
summary: The dollar index jumped about 0.8% to near 102.26, its biggest one-day gain since June, after October payrolls rose 165,000 against a 65,000 forecast and pushed December Fed hike odds back toward 80%. The rupee led on cheaper oil and foreign inflows and the Taiwan dollar recovered on official support, while the Aussie, loonie, pound and euro lagged and the won slid on another day of record-scale foreign selling.
drivers: US payrolls revive the December Fed hike

Payrolls rose 165,000 against a 65,000 forecast, unemployment fell to 4.1% and wages rose 0.4%, so two-year Treasury yields rose about 4bp to 4.52% and December hike odds climbed back toward 80% from about 67%. Williams, Musalem and Daly all leaned hawkish, and the euro fell about 0.7% to near 1.1143.
Data divergence hits the loonie and Aussie

Canada lost 4,700 jobs against a 13,600 gain expected and unemployment rose to 6.7%, cutting BoC December hike odds to about 35%, so USD/CAD jumped about 0.8% to near 1.4130. The Aussie fell about 0.9% to near 0.6868, its lowest since late March and down about 2.5% on the week, as a paused RBA met a hawkish Fed.
AI rout drains Asian equities, officials step in

Foreigners sold about 2.8tn won of Korean shares as the Kospi fell 6%, pushing the won to 1,356.6 in Seoul. Taiwan's stock index entered a bear market, but the Taiwan dollar rebounded from 33.04 to 32.768 as state banks sold dollars and a stabilisation fund was activated.
view: Bullish for the next 1–2 weeks: payrolls broke the DXY above 102.20, the Fed is priced to hike in December while the RBA and BoC look done, and AI-driven outflows keep weighing on Asian currencies. I back the dollar on dips against the loonie, Aussie, euro and won, and fade it only against the yen near Tokyo's 159–160 line. A DXY close back below 101.50, or soft US October inflation, would turn me neutral.
ideas: Buy 1.4080–1.4100 as Canada sheds jobs and the Fed stays on track to hike; for 1.4250, stop 1.4020.
Sell 0.6900–0.6920 now that the RBA has paused and the Fed has not; for 0.6780, stop 0.6970.
Buy 1,353–1,357 while foreigners keep dumping Korean chip stocks; for 1,385, stop 1,342.
review: The AUD/USD sale at 0.6970–0.6990 never filled but the pair fell to about 0.6868, near the 0.6850 target, so I reset the entry; the USD/JPY sale filled near 158.4 and is flat, and the won buy narrowly missed its entry before the won slid to 1,356.6. I close the USD/TWD long at about 32.77 (about 0.13 against me) after officials defended 33, and the ringgit sale near flat at about 4.06 after payrolls; EUR/USD, USD/CAD and USD/INR broke their ranges, so those calls change, and the rupiah long is slightly in favour.

eurusd.note: Down about 0.7% to near 1.1143, its biggest drop since Oct 1, breaking the 1.1150 range floor.
eurusd.why: The dollar did the moving. October payrolls rose 165,000, more than double the forecast, with unemployment at 4.1% and wages up 0.4%, so two-year Treasury yields rose to about 4.52% and December Fed hike odds climbed back toward 80%. The euro was already soft on haven demand as the AI selloff spread to Europe, and the data turned that into its biggest one-day fall in five weeks.
eurusd.outlook: I turn bearish: the 1.1150–1.1300 range broke and rate spreads favour the dollar, so I sell rallies to 1.1170–1.1190 for 1.1050. A close above 1.1260 would end the call.
eurusd.watch: US October inflation, Fed speakers, ECB speakers ahead of December, euro-zone sentiment data.

view.call: Sell 1.1170–1.1190; Fed hike back on, range broke.

gbpusd.note: Down about 0.75% to near 1.3347, its biggest fall since Sept 23, after Thursday's seven-week high.
gbpusd.why: The dollar did most of the moving after the strong US jobs report, and sterling gave back its post-BoE gains. The pound had hit a seven-week high on Thursday after the BoE's hike to 4%, but with about 100bp of further hikes already priced, the stronger US data and a revived December Fed hike left little room for more. It still fell less than the Aussie and loonie because gilt yields stay high.
gbpusd.outlook: I lower the range to 1.3280–1.3480: BoE hike pricing supports dips, but a hawkish Fed caps rallies. A close below 1.3280 would open 1.3200.
gbpusd.watch: UK Q3 GDP, UK labour data, BoE speakers, US October inflation.

view.call: 1.3280–1.3480; hawkish BoE vs a hawkish Fed.

audusd.note: Down about 0.9% to near 0.6868, its lowest since late March; down about 2.5% on the week.
audusd.why: Both sides moved against the Aussie. The RBA's split 6–3 hike to 4.85% dropped its tightening bias and markets now see no further hikes for months, while the strong US payrolls report revived a December Fed hike. The Aussie is also the market's proxy for Asian tech, and it slid as Korea's Kospi fell 6% and Taiwan's index entered a bear market.
audusd.outlook: I stay bearish and reset the entry: sell rallies to 0.6900–0.6920 for 0.6780, as rate spreads now favour the dollar. A close above 0.6970 would end the call.
audusd.watch: Australia jobs data, China trade and inflation data, AI-stock sentiment, US October inflation.

view.call: Sell 0.6900–0.6920; RBA paused, Fed still hiking.

usdjpy.note: Up about 0.5% to near 158.43, undoing Thursday's yen gain; the sale filled near 158.4.
usdjpy.why: The dollar did most of the moving as payrolls lifted Treasury yields and Fed hike bets, and the yen's haven bid faded as the Nasdaq rallied more than 1%. Prime Minister Takaichi's plan to spend proceeds from the BoJ's ETF sales on her investment projects added to fiscal worries, while Governor Ueda said underlying inflation should stay near 2% with some upside risks.
usdjpy.outlook: I keep the sale from 158.20–158.50 for 156.50: Tokyo's 159–160 line limits the upside and the BoJ still leans toward a December hike. A close above 159.40 would end the call.
usdjpy.watch: Japan wage data, Tokyo comments near 159–160, BoJ speakers, US October inflation.

view.call: Short from 158.20–158.50; Tokyo's 160 line, BoJ hawkish.

usdchf.note: Up about 0.45% to near 0.8200, back in the middle of its 0.8130–0.8280 range.
usdchf.why: The dollar did the moving. Haven demand that had lifted the franc on Thursday faded as US stocks steadied and the Nasdaq rallied more than 1%, and the strong payrolls report pushed US yields and Fed hike bets higher. Low Swiss inflation keeps the SNB on hold, so the franc's rate gap with the dollar widened again.
usdchf.outlook: I keep the 0.8130–0.8280 range: a hawkish Fed lifts the pair, but the franc still draws haven demand on any new equity slide. A close above 0.8280 would open 0.8350.
usdchf.watch: SNB sight deposits (Nov 9), Swiss inflation, US October inflation, equity sentiment.

usdcad.note: Up about 0.8% to near 1.4130, a near three-week high, breaking the 1.4080 range top.
usdcad.why: Both sides moved. Canada lost 4,700 jobs in October against a 13,600 gain expected, unemployment rose to a six-month high of 6.7% and BoC December hike odds fell to about 35%, while US payrolls beat by about 100,000. Oil gave no help: Brent ended near $98, still down about 16% on the week.
usdcad.outlook: I turn bullish: the jobs gap points to a hiking Fed and a paused BoC, so I buy dips to 1.4080–1.4100 for 1.4250. A close below 1.4020 would end the call.
usdcad.watch: Canada inflation and BoC speakers, US October inflation, oil and US-Iran talks.

view.call: Buy 1.4080–1.4100; Canada jobs fall, Fed set to hike.

usdcnh.note: Yuan slightly weaker near 6.674 after a softer PBOC fixing at 6.7168; first weekly loss in six weeks.
usdcnh.why: Beijing and the dollar both pushed the same way. The PBOC set the midpoint at 6.7168, weaker than Thursday's 6.7156 and about 400 pips weaker than the Reuters estimate of 6.6762, a clear sign it wants slower gains. Falling Chinese stocks weighed in Asia, and the stronger dollar after payrolls kept the yuan soft in New York.
usdcnh.outlook: I keep the 6.64–6.70 range: the PBOC is leaning against gains while exporters still sell dollars on rallies. A close above 6.70 would show Beijing wants a weaker yuan.
usdcnh.watch: Daily fixings vs estimates, China trade and inflation data, FX reserve ratio rise (Nov 15).

view.call: 6.64–6.70; PBOC slows the yuan, dollar firm.

usdhkd.note: Little changed near 7.840, still near the weak end of the 7.75–7.85 band.
usdhkd.why: Nothing local moved the pair. The gap between Hong Kong interbank rates and US rates still favours holding US dollars, and stronger Fed hike bets after payrolls keep that gap wide. Equity swings in Hong Kong made little difference to the peg.
usdhkd.outlook: No trade in 7.83–7.85: the carry gap keeps it near 7.85, and only a jump in HIBOR or HKMA buying at 7.85 would pull it lower.
usdhkd.watch: HKMA operations at 7.85, HIBOR, US October inflation.

view.call: 7.83–7.85, no trade; carry gap keeps it near 7.85.

usdsgd.note: Up about 0.3% to near 1.2825, in the upper half of its range after the payrolls jump.
usdsgd.why: The dollar did the moving. It was already firm in Asia on haven demand, with Singapore stocks down 2.8% as banks slid on weaker profits, and then gained on the strong payrolls report. The Singapore dollar still lost far less than the euro or Aussie because the S$NEER policy band limits its swings.
usdsgd.outlook: I keep the 1.2740–1.2860 range: the firmer dollar favours the top half, but MAS's appreciating band limits gains. A close above 1.2860 would open 1.2920.
usdsgd.watch: US October inflation, Singapore Q3 GDP, Asian tech-stock flows.

usdkrw.note: Won fell 14.5 to 1,356.6 in Seoul, weakest daytime close since late Sept; about 1,364 offshore.
usdkrw.why: The won did the moving. Foreigners sold about 2.8tn won of Kospi shares as the index fell 6% after a circuit breaker, and the conversion of those proceeds into dollars hit the won. The strong US payrolls report then lifted the dollar, taking the offshore rate to about 1,364.
usdkrw.outlook: I stay bullish and lift the entry: buy dips to 1,353–1,357 for 1,385 while foreign selling of chip stocks continues. A close below 1,342 would end the call.
usdkrw.watch: Foreign Kospi flows, Korean authorities' comments, AI-chip sentiment, US October inflation.

usdtwd.note: Taiwan dollar rebounded 10.8 cents to 32.768 in Taipei after hitting 33.04, weakest since April 2025.
usdtwd.why: Officials did the moving. The Taiwan dollar first broke through 33 as the stock index fell as much as 8.9% and entered a bear market, but state banks and exporters sold dollars, the stabilisation fund was cleared to buy shares and regulators tightened short-selling rules. Foreigners have sold a net NT$524bn of Taiwan shares this month after a record October.
usdtwd.outlook: I close the long and switch to a 32.60–33.05 range: officials are clearly defending 33, but foreign selling still pressures dips. A close above 33.05 would show the defence has failed.
usdtwd.watch: Foreign Taiex flows, stabilisation fund buying, TSMC October sales (Nov 10), central bank action.

usdmyr.note: Ringgit gave back Thursday's gain, slipping to 4.0565/0610 at the 6pm close from 4.0445/0490.
usdmyr.why: The dollar did the moving. Safe-haven demand for the dollar spread to Asian currencies as chip stocks slid again, and the ringgit gave back the gain it made after Bank Negara held at 2.75%. The strong US payrolls report later in the day added to pressure on Asian currencies.
usdmyr.outlook: I close the sale at about 4.06, roughly flat, and move to a 4.035–4.085 range: Bank Negara's steady stance supports the ringgit, but a firmer dollar limits gains.
usdmyr.watch: Malaysia trade data and Q3 GDP, regional chip stocks, US October inflation.

usdphp.note: Peso eased 8.5 centavos to 63.055 at the BAP close but gained about 1.1% on the week.
usdphp.why: The peso gave back a little of Thursday's jump as the dollar firmed on haven demand in Asia. Cheaper oil and seasonal dollar sales by overseas workers and exporters ahead of Christmas kept losses small, and October's 7.8% inflation keeps a BSP hike in December in play. The payrolls jump came after Manila had closed.
usdphp.outlook: I keep the 62.70–63.50 range: BSP hike bets and remittance season support the peso, but a firmer dollar limits gains. A close above 63.50 would put 64 back in view.
usdphp.watch: Philippine Q3 GDP, BSP comments, oil, US October inflation, BSP decision (Dec 17).

view.call: 62.70–63.50; BSP hike bets vs firmer dollar.

usdidr.note: Rupiah slipped 7 points to 18,089 after trading between about 18,070 and 18,140.
usdidr.why: The rupiah gave up a little of Thursday's gain as global risk aversion hit Asian assets. Strong third-quarter growth of 5.47% and reserves rising to $146.8bn limited the damage, and Bank Indonesia is seen smoothing moves. The payrolls jump came after Jakarta closed, so Monday should open weaker.
usdidr.outlook: I keep the long, slightly in favour, for 18,300: the stronger dollar and steady outflows outweigh solid growth. A close below 18,060 would end the call.
usdidr.watch: Bank Indonesia operations, foreign bond flows, US October inflation.

usdinr.note: Rupee jumped 56 paise to 93.91, a six-and-a-half-month high and Asia's best performer.
usdinr.why: The rupee did the moving. Foreign investors bought Indian shares as India stood apart from the AI selloff, and Brent's roughly 16% weekly drop cuts India's import bill. The RBI was seen buying dollars near 93.88, which capped gains, and the payrolls jump came after Mumbai had closed.
usdinr.outlook: I lower the range to 93.50–94.50: cheaper oil and inflows favour the rupee, but RBI dollar buying and a firmer global dollar limit gains. A Brent close back above $105 would push it toward 94.50.
usdinr.watch: Oil and US-Iran talks, RBI dollar buying, foreign flows, India inflation data.

view.call: 93.50–94.50; oil and inflows vs RBI buying.

eurjpy.note: Down about 0.2% to near 176.5 as the euro fell more than the yen; mid-range.
eurjpy.why: Both legs weakened against the dollar after payrolls, but the euro fell further. The euro lost about 0.7% to the dollar while the yen lost about 0.5% as its haven bid faded and Tokyo's fiscal plans weighed, leaving the cross a little lower.
eurjpy.outlook: I keep the 175.5–178.0 range: a hawkish BoJ and haven demand cap rallies, while yen fiscal worries limit dips. A close below 175.5 would open 174.
eurjpy.watch: Tokyo comments, Japan wage data, ECB speakers, equity sentiment.

view.call: 175.5–178.0; both legs soft vs the dollar.

cnhjpy.note: Up about 0.4% to near 23.74 as the yen fell more than the yuan.
cnhjpy.why: The yen did the moving. It lost about 0.5% to the dollar as its haven bid faded and payrolls lifted US yields, while the yuan slipped only slightly after a weaker PBOC fixing at 6.7168. That pushed the cross into the upper half of its range.
cnhjpy.outlook: I keep the 23.3–23.9 range: Beijing is slowing the yuan and the yen still has haven support, so neither leg should run far.
cnhjpy.watch: PBOC fixings, China inflation data, FX reserve ratio rise (Nov 15), Tokyo comments.

watch: Next: US October inflation and Fed speakers, China trade and inflation data, TSMC sales (Nov 10), the PBOC's FX reserve hike (Nov 15), the BoE and BSP (Dec 17), plus Tokyo's 159–160 line, Taiwan's defence of 33 and foreign flows out of Asian chip stocks.
